reasoning_log_text: LO evaluations: Local oddballs showed robust, widespread signaling (Fig. 2), contradicting H1 suppression (-0.6 for SST/PV). Local responses showed feedforward progression (Fig. 2b, 2c), supporting H2 (+0.6 for Ascending Latency Shift). Inhibitory interneurons did not modulate GOs (Fig. 4d), contradicting H1 (-0.6 for SST/PV). GO responses were sparse and restricted to higher-order areas (Fig. 3a, 3b), contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Feedforward Error Propagation). LO signaling was ubiquitous (Fig. 2a, 3), supporting H3 (+0.6 for Hierarchical Activity Ubiquity). GO signaling was found to be more consistent with feedback than feedforward (Fig. 5b, GC analysis), contradicting H2 (-0.6 for Feedforward Non-local Directed Connectivity). GO signaling was restricted to higher-order areas, supporting a specific form of H3 (+0.6 for Hierarchical Presence). GO detection was sparse across units (Fig. 3b), contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Population-Wide Ubiquity). GO responses were laminar/area specific, contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Canonical Microcircuit Ubiquity). GO latency did not scale hierarchically (Fig. 3c), contradicting H2 (-0.6 for Ascending Latency Shift). GO signaling was restricted to extragranular layers in mice, contradicting H2 (-0.6 for Feedforward Non-local Supragranular Activity (L2/3)). GO activity was not found in L2/3 of mice, contradicting H2 (-0.6 for Feedforward Non-local Supragranular Activity (L2/3)). GO detection was sparse across units, contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Population-Wide Ubiquity). GO response was found to be more consistent with feedback than feedforward, contradicting H2 (-0.6 for Feedforward Error Propagation). GO signaling was restricted to higher-order areas, contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Hierarchical Mechanism Invariance). GO responses were not found to be ubiquitous across all areas/species (Fig. 3b), contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Hierarchical Activity Ubiquity). GO signaling was not observed in L2/3 of mice, contradicting H2 (-0.6 for Feedforward Non-local Supragranular Activity (L2/3)). GO signaling was not found to be consistent across all layers, contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Hierarchical CSD Ubiquity). GO detection was sparse across units, contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Population-Wide Ubiquity). GO detection was not found to be ubiquitous across all areas, contradicting H3 (-0.6 for Hierarchical Presence (V1-PFC)). GO detection was not found to be consistent across all brain states, contradicting H3 (-0.6 for State-Independent Ubiquity).
